skill.name: frontend-security-coder
skill.description: Expert in secure frontend coding practices specializing in XSS prevention, output sanitization, and client-side security patterns.
skill.summary: Guides secure frontend implementation for XSS prevention, CSP, sanitization, secure navigation, and browser security controls.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Frontend code can expose users to XSS, unsafe redirects, and browser security gaps. This skill guides secure UI changes with focused frontend security patterns.
actual_capabilities: Recommends safe DOM manipulation patterns for dynamic and user-generated content.
Guides DOMPurify and sanitizer use for rich text and markdown rendering.
Supports CSP planning with nonces, hashes, report-only rollout, and source restrictions.
Covers URL validation, open redirect prevention, and secure link handling.
Advises on browser controls such as SRI, Trusted Types, and referrer policy.
Helps secure frontend authentication flows, token storage, and session behavior.
limitations: It does not replace a full application security audit.
It cannot verify production headers without project access and runtime testing.
It focuses on frontend risks, not backend authorization or infrastructure security.
Generated guidance still needs review against framework and browser requirements.

use_cases.title: Harden User Content Rendering
use_cases.description: Apply safe rendering patterns for comments, profiles, markdown, and rich text areas.

use_cases.title: Plan CSP Deployment
use_cases.description: Create a practical CSP rollout using report-only mode, nonces, hashes, and source restrictions.

use_cases.title: Review Product Flows
use_cases.description: Check redirects, third-party widgets, authentication screens, and payment forms for client-side weaknesses.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Frontend Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one UI feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this frontend feature for XSS, unsafe URLs, and insecure DOM updates. Explain the risks and safer changes.

prompt_templates.title: Secure User Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me render user-generated content safely. Include sanitizer choices, allowed content rules, and testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CSP Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CSP rollout for this app. Include report-only testing, nonce or hash choices, third-party sources, and migration steps.

prompt_templates.title: Threat Model a Client Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Threat model this frontend flow. Cover XSS, clickjacking, open redirects, token handling, third-party scripts, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Review a comment widget that inserts user text into the page.
output: Use text-only insertion for plain comments and avoid HTML rendering.
If rich text is required, sanitize with a maintained library and strict allowlists.
Add tests for script tags, event handlers, unsafe links, and malformed markup.

output_examples.input: Plan a CSP for a React application with analytics and a payment widget.
output: Start with report-only mode and collect violations before enforcement.
Use nonces or hashes for scripts and remove inline event handlers.
Restrict third-party sources to approved analytics and payment domains.

output_examples.input: Improve a redirect parameter used after login.
output: Replace free-form URLs with destination identifiers or an allowlist.
Reject external protocols and normalize paths before navigation.
Add tests for encoded URLs, protocol-relative URLs, and nested redirects.

best_practices: Share the framework, browser targets, and relevant code before asking for implementation guidance.
Ask for verification steps, including unit tests, browser checks, and security header validation.
Use the skill before adding third-party scripts, rich text, redirects, or authentication UI.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to approve unsafe HTML rendering without sanitization.
Do not treat client-side validation as the only protection for sensitive actions.
Do not deploy CSP changes without report-only testing and monitoring.

faq.question: What does this skill help secure?
faq.answer: It helps secure frontend code, browser policies, DOM updates, redirects, widgets, and client-side authentication flows.

faq.question: Can it replace a penetration test?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and review support, but it does not replace hands-on security testing.

faq.question: Does it only cover XSS?
faq.answer: No. It also covers CSP, clickjacking, redirects, token handling, third-party scripts, and browser security features.

faq.question: Can it write framework-specific fixes?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the framework, component code, and constraints so it can tailor secure changes.

faq.question: Does it require network or command access?
faq.answer: No. The skill is prompt guidance and does not include executable code.

faq.question: How should teams verify its suggestions?
faq.answer: Review changes manually, run tests, inspect browser behavior, and validate headers in the target environment.
